caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1536 of 2014
lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Md. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Dr. A.T.M. Mizanur Rahman ------- Petitioner
VS
Ali Hossain and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
6. Against the said order of dismissal of the suit for default, the plaintiff instead of filing an application under Order XI, rule 9 of the Code, filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 05 of 2009 before the District Judge, Bhola. The learned Additional District Judge, Bhola by his judgment and order dated 23.02.2014 dismissed the same. The judgment and order of the learned Additional District Judge was challenged by the plaintiff by filing a revision application before the High Court Division under section 115(1) of the Code and a learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned order summarily disposed of the same treating the memorandum of appeal of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 05 of 2009 as an application under "Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure to be numbered and treated as miscellaneous case for restoration of the title suit in its original file and number as per provision of Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure after observing all necessary legal procedure and formalities" and directed the District Judge, Bhola "to transmit and send the memorandum of appeal" of the miscellaneous appeal (5 of 2009) to the Court of the Joint District Judge, Bhola "to accept the same and treat the same as an application under Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereafter to proceed with the same as per law for restoration of the Title Suit No. 40 of 1994 which was dismissed for default on 17.05.2009". The learned Judge of the Single Bench also directed the parties to maintain status quo in respect of possession of the suit land for a period of 01 (one) year "pending hearing and disposal of the Miscellaneous Case"; hence this petition for leave to appeal. 

 7. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner, has submitted that time and again, this Court has disapproved summary disposal of a revision application under section 115 of the Code giving full relief to the petitioner without issuing the Rule and thus giving no opportunity to the other side (s) of being heard and the last pronouncement on the subject was made in the case of Gulf Air Company (GSC) and another-Vs- Travel Trade Limited and others, 65 DLR (AD), 141. He has further submitted that the miscellaneous appeal filed before the District Judge being incompetent in law and the same having been dismissed the question of treating the memorandum of appeal of the said appeal as an application under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code for restoration of the suit dismissed for default, does not arise at all, the learned Judge of the Single Bench committed a prima facie error in passing the impugned order and as such, the same calls for interference by this Court by giving leave. 

 9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the learned Advocate-on-Record for the plaintiff-respondent, the order of the learned Joint District Judge dismissing the suit for default and the impugned order of the High Court Division. So far as the summary disposal of the revision application under section 115 of the Code giving full relief to the petitioner without issuing the Rule is concerned, this Court in the case of Gulf Air Company (GSC) and another (supra) has in unequivocal language observed that This tendency of giving relief in a summary manner without hearing the other side(s) is clearly violative of the law declared by this Division and the principles of natural Justi6e as well". In that case, this Court further held that "However, we reiterate the statement of law that summary disposal of a revision application filed under section 115 of the Code giving full relief to the petitioner without issuing Rule and thus giving no opportunity to the other side(s) of being heard is not permissible. We strongly disapprove and deprecate such kind of disposal by the High Court Division." In view of the provisions of article 111 of the Constitution, the High Court Division was obliged to follow the said pronouncement of this Division. But unfortunately, it appears to us, the High Court Division gave a deaf ear to the pronouncement of this Division. We fail to understand what more strict language can be used to make the High Court Division understood that it is constitutionally bound to follow the pronouncement of this Division. In view of the above, we are not required to restate the law on the point except that the order of the High Court Division in disposing of the revision application summarily giving full relief to the petitioner without issuing the Rule is deplorable and the same cannot be sustained. 

 10. So far as the treating of the memorandum of appeal of Miscellaneous Appeal No.5 of 2009 as an application under Order XI, rule 9 of the Code and also as a miscellaneous case for restoration of the suit to its original file and number as per the said provision of the Code is concerned, is absolutely contrary to law. This will be clear if we look at the provisions of law as codified in the Code in this regard. Order IX of the Code has dealt with the exigencies of the appearance of parties and consequence of non appearance. Admittedly the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing on 17.05.2009 and as the plaintiff did not turn up on repeated calls, the same was dismissed for default. Relevant rules of Order XI as to the dismissal of the suit for default and its restoration setting aside the order of dismissal if the plaintiff elects to apply for such restoration are rules 8 and 9 which read as follows: 

 "8. Where the defendant appears and the plaintiff does not appear when the suit is called on for hearing, the Court shall made an order that the suit be dismissed, unless the defendant admits the claim, or part thereof, in which case the Court shall pass a decree against the defendant upon such admission and, where part only of the claim has been admitted, shall dismiss the suit so far as it relates to the remainder. 

 11. There should not be any doubt that the instant suit was dismissed for default under rule 8 of Order IX of the Code, when the same was called on for hearing, the plaintiff did not appear. A mere reading of rule 9 of Order IX of the Code shows that where a suit is dismissed wholly or partly under rule 8 thereof the plain-tiff shall be precluded from bringing a fresh suit in respect of the same cause of action, but he may apply for an order to set the dismissal aside. But instead of filing an application under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code to set aside the order of dismissal of the suit, the plaintiff filed the miscellaneous appeal before the District Judge. Of course, the plaintiff could also file an application under the provisions of Order XLVII, rule I of the Code for reviewing the order dismissing the suit for default. 

 12. The orders, against which an appeal shall lie, have been enumerated in clauses (a)-(w) of rule 1, Order XLIII of the Code. In none of those clauses, an order dismissing the suit for default under rule 8 of Order IX has been made appealable. It may be stated that clause (c) of rule 1 of Order XLIII has provided for an appeal against an order under rule 9 of Order IX rejecting an application (in a case open to appeal). And it does not require any elucidation for the legal proposition that appeal is a creature of the statue and no appeal can be filed to any authority, be it judicial or quasi judicial or administrative, unless such an appeal is provided for in the relevant statute. So, the appeal filed by the plaintiff before the District Judge, Bhola against the order of dismissal of the suit under Order IX, rule 8 of the Code was absolutely incompetent and consequently not maintainable and was liable to be dismissed in limine. The Single Bench also found the appeal as a misconceived one. It observed: 

 "It is very clear from the impugned Judgment and order and after going through the revisional application and the ground taken therein that the filing of the miscellaneous appeal was totally a misconceived idea." 

 13. So, when the miscellaneous appeal in question was incompetent treating its memorandum of appeal as an application under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code and to be numbered and treated as miscellaneous case for restoration of the title suit in its original file and number as per provision of Order IX rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure after observing all necessary legal procedure and formalities as observed and directed by the High Court Division does not arise at all, such observations and directions of the High Court Division are totally misconceived, and also contrary to law. Moreso, there was no existence of any appeal after the same was dismissed by the learned Additional District Judge on being transferred to him for disposal. 

 14. In giving the direction to treat the memorandum of appeal of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 5 of 2009 as an application under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code, the Single Bench totally failed to consider article 163 of the Limitation Act which has provided limitation for a period 30 days to file an application by the plaintiff for an order to set aside a dismissal order. Admittedly, when the Single Bench disposed of the revision application summarily, period of 30 days expired long before, but it gave the direction upon the Joint District Judge to accept the memorandum of appeal of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 05 of 2009 as an application under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code and to proceed with the same as per law for restoration of the suit giving a clear go by to the said provision of the Limitation Act. The Single Bench also failed to consider that a valuable vested legal right accrued to the defendant, the moment, the suit was dismissed for default and that right could not be taken away without hearing him and that without a proper application for condonation of delay under section 5 of the Limitation Act as well. For all these reasons, the treating of the memorandum of appeal by the High Court Division as an application under Order IX, rule 9 of the Code for restoration of the suit to its file and number and the direction given by it upon the District Judge to send the memorandum of appeal to the Joint District Judge concerned with the further direction upon him to accept and treat the same accordingly, cannot be sustained on any legal principle. 

 15. Generally in this kind of order of the High Court Division, we set aside the order of the High Court Division and send the matter back on remand to it for disposal as a motion (here the revision application) on merit in accordance with law, but in the instant case, it would serve no purpose if we follow that general practice and send the matter back on remand to the High Court Division, as the appeal, itself, in which judgment and order impugned in the revision application, was passed, was ex-facie not maintainable. And we are not also inclined to give leave in the matter as that would keep the matter pending before this Court to the woe of the contesting defendant, the suit being of 1994, and one for specific performance of contract. It may be stated that the plaintiff-respondent has very well been represented by Mr. Md. Zahirul Islam, learned Advocate-on-Record.
